items.title: Steve Turré interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 29, 2021
items.q: And when I played with Art Blakey and Max Roach, you know, the same thing

ctx.x: How do you have them work on that? To get more rhythm in their playing?

Well look it. Let’s make an analogy here. If you’re studying harmony you’ve got to start with the root. And once you have three notes you have a chord and then you build off the top of that. But you go back to the root. So it’s the same thing with rhythm. Let’s go to the root. What makes jazz music different than — you see in academia especially in the United States but in Europe too they teach music, even jazz music, they teach it from a European perspective. And yes most of the instruments are European…

response, rhythm is number one. Rhythm. And so you know if I have a student that really has a problem with rhythm I have them pick up some percussion instruments. Learn to play the clave, learn to play a basic rhythm and hold it steady. You’ve got to listen and make it fit like this with the other rhythms. And it breathes. It’s not a metronome like a drum machine. You have to adjust to the ebb and flow of the collective. It’s a collective consciousness. And I put on traditional African drummers and show them…
